prize_parts.citation: for the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is the kind of simple, general, enabling chemistry that I would call a game-changer: it replaced harsh and narrow classical amination methods with a ligand-controlled catalytic reaction that is now routine in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis. The consequences are already demonstrated at industrial scale, the mechanism is understood well enough to guide ligand design, and three decades of independent use leave no doubt about maturity. Three members placed it first in the openings, which I read as agreement on the science rather than a reason to support it. Attribution is cleaner than in most of the shortlist: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalyst systems, which gives two laureates and leaves room under the three-person limit.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize: some colleagues may see this as an extension of the same palladium theme and not a new discovery. There is also the Migita/Kosugi priority question, since the tin-amide coupling preceded the ligand-enabled work, and a second-order worry that the field is a method for a single bond type, which makes it narrower in concept than targeted degradation or sequencing, whose conceptual reach is wider.

responses.point: A two-person Buchwald-Hartwig prize is the cleanest configuration, with Kosugi as a precursor, and the C-N coupling is a natural complement to the 2010 prize.
responses.response: I agree on the configuration, and as a theorist I would add that the mechanistic picture (oxidative addition, amine binding, reductive elimination controlled by ligand bulk) is what made the reaction general and not just empirically useful. I would still ask that we state in the citation that the prize rewards the general catalytic system and not the earlier tin-amide chemistry, so Kosugi's priority is acknowledged in the text rather than only argued around.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues is a new event-driven pharmacology, with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as the core, and it is timely despite clinical approval still pending.
responses.response: I ranked B004 third and I take the conceptual novelty seriously. My reservation is maturity and attribution: no approved PROTAC drug exists yet, so the consequences are promised rather than demonstrated, and the three-name cap forces us to leave out Handa and Ito on the cereblon glue side, which is the strand with an actual marketed drug history through thalidomide analogues. I would not oppose it as a future prize, but I do not think it displaces a mature, fully demonstrated method this year.

responses.point: C-N coupling is a general method that complements the 2010 prize rather than duplicating it, and its recognition is overdue.
responses.response: I agree that it is distinct from the 2010 work, since the key advance is a different bond type enabled by new ligand classes rather than by the original catalytic cycle. I would qualify the claim that it is overdue: being overdue is not itself an argument, and the case rests on demonstrated consequences, which I believe are strong. Where I differ is that I do not think Kosugi's priority can be dismissed as a third name; the committee should be ready to explain why the ligand-enabled generality, not the first observation, is what we are crediting.

responses.point: Base editing by Liu, Komor and Gaudelli is a clear, genuinely new capability with a defined chemical mechanism and rapid uptake, ranked first by the chair.
responses.response: The mechanism is chemically elegant and I ranked it fifth rather than lower for that reason. My reservations are timing and the CRISPR prize of 2020: base editing is roughly a decade old, long-term clinical safety is still accruing, and the committee has recently recognised the genome-editing platform it builds upon. Attribution among Liu, Komor, Gaudelli and the Nishida and Kondo strand also needs a decision about trainee credit that I think is harder than the opening ballots suggest.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats C-N coupling as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
How to acknowledge Migita/Kosugi priority in the citation without adding a third laureate.
Whether degraders (B004) will be considered mature enough this year if no PROTAC drug is approved.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the shortlisted candidates; my connections are to Arieh Warshel and the Uppsala ribosome community, none of whom are credited on the shortlist.
